site.name: civicport
site.summary: civicport-clone Fictional municipal online permit portal "CivicPort · City of Avalon Bay". Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Portal home: three large icon-action buttons (Apply / Track / Pay); service-announcement list | | `apply.html` | Three-column layout: left step tree (6 groups + sub-steps, sub-steps show completed ✓ / current highlight / conditionally locked, completed steps are click-back-able); center current-step form (dynamically rendered: address, project type, scope, dates, parcel lookup, ownership, contractor, various file uploads, neighbor signature block, various affidavits, final review and submit); right sticky "What materials you'll need" dynamic checklist (updates ✓ as you progress / select) + estimated fee breakdown card (with expedited toggle); conditional visibility (exterior changes → neighbor step; historic parcel → historic-district step; Addition/Structural → elevation drawings; Roof/Electrical/HVAC → energy worksheet) | | `my-applications.html` | List of 3 past applications (status badges) |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full civicport system, prioritizing the primary form/onboarding flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The CivicPort application portal offers a structured multi-step flow with helpful real-time progress tracking via the dynamic sidebar checklist. However, significant UX gaps hinder the experience, most notably a complete lack of required field validation and a confusing post-submission state that fails to confirm user success. Additionally, missing programmatic labels on form fields and small touch targets negatively impact accessibility and mobile usability.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore the CivicPort permit application portal, focusing heavily on the dynamic multi-step application form, its conditional logic, and recovery states.
exploration_plan.summary: The run will first map the static pages (Home, Fees, My Applications) to establish baseline navigation. The bulk of the exploration will focus on the `apply.html` form, executing multiple passes to validate the linear 'happy path', trigger conditional steps (like historic district or exterior changes), and test interruption flows like cancellation and backward navigation. Finally, critical interactions will be re-tested in a mobile viewport.
assumptions: The multi-step form in apply.html is entirely client-side rendered via JavaScript based on user input.
The 'What you'll need' checklist and fee estimator update dynamically as form fields are filled.
The application process can be canceled or navigated backward without breaking state.
risk_hotspots: Conditional step rendering in apply.html (ensure steps are correctly added/removed based on specific inputs).
State management of the Cancel dialog in the application flow.
Missing input labels on the first step of apply.html.
Synchronization of the sticky sidebar checklist and fee estimator with form inputs.
Small tap targets across the global navigation.

phases.title: Basic Navigation and Static Content
phases.objective: Verify the global navigation and the content of static auxiliary pages.
key_checks: Click through the top navigation links.
Verify the large icon-action buttons on the homepage work correctly.
Ensure content is fully visible on the Fees and My Applications pages.
exit_criteria: All static pages have been visited and their primary content/links verified.

phases.title: Permit Application - Standard Flow
phases.objective: Execute a standard, non-conditional path through the permit application.
key_checks: Fill out initial steps (address, basic project type).
Verify clicking 'Save and continue' progresses the form and updates the step tree.
Check that the 'What you'll need' checklist updates as steps are completed.
Test clicking the 'Back' button or clicking on completed steps in the tree to navigate backward.
exit_criteria: Successfully navigated through several steps of a basic application and confirmed backward navigation.

phases.title: Permit Application - Conditional Branches
phases.objective: Trigger and validate the conditional logic within the application form.
key_checks: Select inputs known to trigger conditional steps (e.g., exterior changes, historic parcel, Addition/Structural).
Verify new steps appear in the left-hand step tree.
Navigate to these newly revealed steps to ensure they render correctly.
exit_criteria: At least two different conditional form states have been triggered and visualized.

phases.title: Application Form - Interruptions & Edge Cases
phases.objective: Test the robustness of the form against interruptions and check dynamic calculations.
key_checks: Click the 'Cancel' button and interact with the resulting dialog.
Toggle the 'Expedited review' checkbox and verify the 'Estimated Fees' total updates correctly.
Attempt to proceed without filling required fields to check for validation messaging.
exit_criteria: Cancel dialog verified, fee calculator validated, and validation errors (if any) observed.

phases.title: Mobile Responsiveness
phases.objective: Ensure the complex application form and small tap targets are usable on mobile.
key_checks: Verify global navigation menus are accessible on a small viewport.
Check how the three-column layout in apply.html collapses (step tree, form, checklist).
Verify tap targets (buttons, links) are easily clickable without zooming.
exit_criteria: Mobile layout observed for the home page and the first step of the application process.

coverage_targets.features: Exercise the standard flow, conditional logic, fee calculator, and cancellation within the application form.
coverage_targets.mobile: Test global navigation and the initial steps of the application form in a mobile viewport to assess layout collapse.

notes: Pay special attention to the missing input labels reported in the prescan on apply.html, as this could impact accessibility and autonomous navigation.

findings.user_goal: Complete the permit application without omitting necessary information.
findings.problem: The form lacks validation for required fields, allowing users to proceed through steps (and ultimately submit) without providing critical data like project area, document uploads, or lead paint acknowledgements.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Save and continue' on various steps (e.g., Property address, Project scope, Site plan upload, Lead paint disclosure) successfully advances the form even when inputs are completely blank.
findings.why_it_matters: Allowing incomplete submissions will result in rejected permits, creating frustration for users who thought they completed the process correctly and requiring manual follow-up from city staff.
findings.suggestion: Implement client-side validation that prevents progression to the next step if required fields are empty, providing clear, inline error messages indicating what is missing.

findings.user_goal: Feel confident that the permit application was successfully submitted to the city.
findings.problem: Submitting the application redirects the user to the 'My applications' page without any success message, and the newly submitted application does not appear in the recent applications list.
findings.evidence: Chunk 9 notes: "There is no confirmation message (e.g., a toast or banner)... The newly submitted application does not appear in the 'My applications' table."
findings.why_it_matters: The lack of immediate system feedback and missing data persistence breaks user trust. Users will likely assume their submission failed, leading them to reapply unnecessarily or contact support.
findings.suggestion: Display a prominent success banner or toast notification upon redirecting, and ensure the newly submitted permit is immediately visible at the top of the applications table with a 'Pending' status.

findings.user_goal: Understand what information is required in each text input using assistive technologies.
findings.problem: Numerous form input fields have visible text above them but lack programmatic accessible labels.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings and chunk summaries indicate that Street address, City, State/Zip, cost, affected area, and date inputs are missing 'for' attributes linking them to a <label>, or lack an 'aria-label'.
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will not be able to determine what data they are supposed to enter into these fields, creating a severe accessibility barrier that prevents them from using the service.
findings.suggestion: Ensure every form input element has a correctly associated `<label for="inputId">` or a descriptive `aria-label`.

findings.user_goal: Easily tap buttons and links on a mobile device without misclicking.
findings.problem: Multiple interactive elements fall well below the standard 44x44px mobile touch target size.
findings.evidence: Mobile layout warnings show the header navigation links are 26px high, the global 'Cancel' button is 51x18px, radio/checkbox inputs are 13x13px, and the 'Look up' button is 76x36px.
findings.why_it_matters: Small tap targets cause usability friction and frustration on mobile devices, leading to accidental misclicks or difficulty interacting with the form.
findings.suggestion: Increase the dimensions and padding of clickable elements so they meet a minimum hit area of 44x44px on mobile viewports.

findings.user_goal: Return to the homepage easily from any step in the process.
findings.problem: The global navigation lacks an explicit 'Home' link, and the top-left 'CivicPort' logo is not interactive.
findings.evidence: Chunk 1 observes: "The global navigation lacks an explicit 'Home' link, and the top-left 'CivicPort' site logo is not interactive."
findings.why_it_matters: Clicking the site logo to return home is a universal web convention. Without it, users may feel trapped in sub-pages or workflows and have to rely on browser back buttons.
findings.suggestion: Wrap the 'CivicPort' logo text/icon in an anchor tag that links back to `index.html`.

findings.user_goal: Clearly read and associate checkboxes with their respective statements.
findings.problem: Certain checkboxes, such as the final attestation and the lead paint disclosure, are awkwardly positioned directly above the center of the text rather than inline.
findings.evidence: Chunk 7 notes the lead paint checkbox is "awkwardly positioned directly above the center of the label text". Chunk 9 notes the attestation checkbox is "horizontally centered within a wide gray container, while its associated label text... is placed left-aligned on the line below".
findings.why_it_matters: This breaks standard form UI patterns, creating visual clutter and making it slightly harder for users to parse what they are checking off.
findings.suggestion: Align checkboxes inline (e.g., using flexbox) immediately to the left of their corresponding label text, sharing the same vertical baseline.
